hypothesis_title: Opening Inside Put/Call Wall Range Predicts Session Containment
exclusion_reason: Requires valid put_wall and call_wall; OHLC from daily_series
verdict_reason: UNTESTABLE AS DEFINED: Wall width averages $35.93 (~7.3% of underlying), while the typical QQQ daily range is 1.5% and only 7 sessions in the test window had a range exceeding 3.7%. Close-based containment is structurally guaranteed (100% for both inside-open and outside-open groups) because a session would need to move ~$18 ($35.93/2) to breach one wall, which almost never occurs. The diff=0 does not mean walls have no effect — it means this metric cannot measure containment when walls are 5x the typical daily range. Lookahead note: walls use same-day EOD OI; the open is observed before that OI is final.

extra_metrics.review_note: Metric trivially satisfied: wall width ~5x typical daily range. Test cannot distinguish wall-containment from no-wall baseline.

hypothesis_title: Opening Outside Put/Call Wall Range Predicts Same-Direction Continuation
exclusion_reason: Requires valid put_wall and call_wall; OHLC from daily_series
verdict_reason: Rejection confirmed in the claimed direction: 0.0% continuation rate on 15 outside-wall opens (12 above call_wall, 3 below put_wall). All 15 outside-wall opens reversed back inside the wall by close — consistent with walls acting as mean-reversion boundaries, not breakout levels. N=15 is too small for statistical inference (binomial p=1.0000 is misleading for a one-sided test at the claimed threshold; the data goes opposite to the claim). Lookahead note: walls use same-day EOD OI; the open classification may be slightly contaminated. p_binomial is one-sided (alternative: rate > 50%).

extra_metrics.review_note: 100% reversal rate (opposite of continuation hypothesis) on n=15 outside-open days. Suggestive of wall-as-resistance but too few events for statistical confidence.

hypothesis_title: Rising Price With Rising Open Interest Predicts Next-Session Continuation

Mann-Whitney p=0.9248 (one-sided, alternative: rising > falling) — strongly inconsistent with the claimed direction. Two-sided p ≈ 0.15 (inconclusive for the reverse claim). Methodological note: total_oi includes 0DTE contracts (created and expired same day in QQQ), making oi_change a noisy proxy for multi-day institutional positioning. The result may reflect 0DTE turnover patterns rather than persistent positioning.

verdict_reason: Rejected (corrected test — Friday filter applied): win_rate=40.5%% on 37 expiry Fridays (n=37, wins=15, p_binomial=0.9061 one-sided). Price moves AWAY from max pain more often than toward it. Mean dist: open=8.794 -> close=10.161 (improvement=-1.367). No max-pain magnetism on weekly expiry Fridays. BUG FIX NOTE: Prior run used n=190 (all sessions) because QQQ has 0DTE options every day; has_expiry=True for all 190 dates. Corrected to filter dayofweek==4 (Fridays only).

verdict_reason: diff=0.0034 (mean_put_heavy=0.0005, mean_control=-0.0029), p_mannwhitney=0.5956, n_signal=47, n_control=47. Thresholds data-driven: signal=PCR≥p75(0.5425), control=PCR≤p25(0.4950). QQQ aggregate PCR clusters in 0.43–0.61; fixed 0.58/0.42 thresholds produce empty groups. Same-day vol confound: 0DTE put volume spikes on large down days mechanically inflate PCR on days when IV tends to rise regardless. Association may reflect coincident conditions rather than PCR predicting IV. Treat as exploratory.

hypothesis_title: Near-Spot Short-Dated OI Concentration Predicts Next-Session Range Contraction

Dealer gamma sign unknown — concentration may dampen (long gamma) or amplify (short gamma) depending on dealer position direction.

hypothesis_title: Peak Gamma-Weighted OI Strike: Proximity Associates with Next-Day Range Contraction
exclusion_reason: Requires C+P param files; EOD close + next-day range from daily_series
verdict_reason: median_range_diff=-0.00654 (near=0.00981, far=0.01634), p_mannwhitney=0.0013, n_near=107, n_far=16. Gross gamma-weighted OI only — dealer position sign unknown. Do not interpret as net dealer gamma or GEX. This is an empirical proximity test; high gamma-OI at a strike means concentrated option sensitivity, not a known directional hedge.
